summary: Add a local persistent highscore store, a finished-run recording path, and a menu panel. Reuse ApoIcarus’s parallel record model and descending-score presentation while replacing its remote service dependency with bounded local-file persistence.
limitations: The requested angle name highlevel is not permitted by the supplied schema.json, whose allowed values are dataflow, requirements, and catalog; requirements is used to remain schema-valid.
The guidance is intentionally unanchored per the task’s high-level-angle instructions; repository-specific symbol and line evidence is therefore not included.

nodes.label: Finished-run record containing actual score, player name, and survival time
Persistent leaderboard and its score ordering
Highscore menu panel and its displayed records
Level-end recording
nodes.untrusted_input: Player name and mutable level/player state at a cleared or lost level
nodes.source: The running game and local player-controlled or tampered game state
nodes.sink: The operation that receives a new highscore record

nodes.label: Leaderboard persistence
nodes.untrusted_input: Stored leaderboard bytes, including records and fields
nodes.sink: The highscore store’s parser and in-memory records

nodes.label: Menu presentation
nodes.untrusted_input: Records loaded from the local store
nodes.sink: The dedicated menu highscore panel and its renderer

nodes.label: A tampered local game state or player name could create a false finished-run record if the level-end integration records values without domain validation.
nodes.task_relevance: Protects the requirement that the board reflects the run’s actual non-negative score, player name, and elapsed time.

nodes.label: Malformed or oversized local store content could corrupt the leaderboard, consume excessive resources, or make the menu unusable if persistence input is read without bounds and structural validation.
nodes.task_relevance: Protects persistence across runs and continued availability of the menu panel.

nodes.label: At the level-end integration point, record exactly one finished run for both level clearing and losing, using the level’s final player score, player name, and elapsed survival time rather than a preview, default, or remote value.
nodes.task_relevance: Provides the feature’s primary effect: recording the real result of every completed run.

nodes.label: At the operation that receives a new record, accept only a non-negative integer score, a non-negative integer survival time, and a name that is non-null, non-blank after trimming, and at most 32 characters; display the accepted duration as mm:ss.
nodes.task_relevance: Defines the input contract for storeRun and prevents invalid values from entering the leaderboard.

nodes.label: Keep accepted records in the supplied local file so that a later highscore-store construction restores the same leaderboard records and their score, name, and survival-time association.
nodes.task_relevance: Satisfies persistence across application runs without assuming a web endpoint.

nodes.label: When records are retained or exposed to the panel, sort complete records by score descending while moving each name and survival time with its score.
nodes.task_relevance: Satisfies the required leaderboard ordering and prevents mismatched displayed fields.

nodes.label: Expose the leaderboard through a dedicated menu panel that displays each retained player name, score, and survival time and can be reached from the game menu.
nodes.task_relevance: Integrates the highscore board into the game’s existing menu/view flow.

nodes.label: Bound the leaderboard to 10 displayed records, bound each stored name to 32 characters, and bound each serialized record to 256 bytes; retain valid records by evicting records beyond the display capacity rather than rejecting a valid record that fits the input contract.
nodes.task_relevance: Keeps the local store and menu sized to the feature while preserving valid run recording.

nodes.label: Use a local, explicitly structured persistence format for the Path-backed store and do not introduce network submission or general object deserialization for highscore records.
nodes.task_relevance: Fits the desktop-game threat model and limits the attack surface while reusing the donor’s record and presentation concepts.

nodes.label: At the receiving record operation, reject and report a null/blank/overlong name or a negative score or duration; before calling it, the level-end integration trims the name and substitutes a stated safe default name for missing or invalid player-name data so the run is still recorded.
nodes.failure_behavior: The store rejects invalid input and reports the rejection; the caller normalizes or defaults missing name data before invoking it.
nodes.task_relevance: Enforces R1 and R2 while preserving the level-end recording effect.

nodes.label: Make the level-end path idempotent for a finished run and invoke it from the common clear/loss transition after final scoring and elapsed-time calculation.
nodes.failure_behavior: A repeated transition does not create duplicate records, while the first valid transition still records the run.
nodes.task_relevance: Ensures R1 records the actual final result exactly once for either end condition.

nodes.label: Parse the local store with an explicit format, reject malformed records, and report parse failures without coercing, clamping, or partially accepting invalid fields.
nodes.failure_behavior: The parser rejects and reports the invalid record; the caller uses an empty valid in-memory leaderboard so the menu remains available.
nodes.task_relevance: Enforces R3 and R7 against edited or corrupted store content.

nodes.label: Apply a byte limit before reading each serialized record and field, and stop reading beyond the configured store budget instead of allocating from unbounded input.
nodes.failure_behavior: Oversized input is rejected and reported; existing valid records remain usable and the panel still opens.
nodes.task_relevance: Enforces R6 against oversized local-file input.

nodes.label: Maintain at most 10 retained records by evicting the lowest-ranked records after insertion, then expose aligned name, score, and survival-time collections in descending score order.
nodes.failure_behavior: Only excess low-ranked records are evicted; the newly accepted valid record is not rejected solely because the board is full.
nodes.task_relevance: Enforces R4 and R6 without costing a valid run that fits the record contract.

nodes.label: Persist through a bounded local-file writer using an explicit text or primitive-value format and atomic replacement where supported, rather than a general object deserializer or remote request.
nodes.failure_behavior: A write failure is reported and the in-memory accepted record remains available for the current panel; no remote submission or unsafe deserialization is attempted.
nodes.task_relevance: Enforces R3 and R7 while adapting the donor implementation to the Path-backed desktop feature.

nodes.label: Have the menu panel render only the bounded, validated store view and format survival time from non-negative seconds as mm:ss without reinterpreting or reordering fields during drawing.
nodes.failure_behavior: Invalid or unavailable rows are omitted from the rendered view while the dedicated panel remains navigable and displays the remaining valid rows.
nodes.task_relevance: Enforces R4, R5, and R6 at the display boundary.
